smt-2012-geometry-tiebreaker-01.title: Right angle at C
smt-2012-geometry-tiebreaker-01.body:
Both smaller triangles contain a right angle (at the foot $D$) and are similar to $ABC$, so $ABC$ is right-angled, and since $\angle A,\angle B$ are acute the right angle is at $C$. Write $a,b,c$ for the sides, $c=AB$. Then $AD=\frac{b^2}c$, $BD=\frac{a^2}c$, $CD=\frac{ab}c$ must be integers.

Write $(a,b,c)=k(x,y,z)$ with $(x,y,z)$ a primitive Pythagorean triple. Then $\frac{b^2}c=\frac{ky^2}{z}$ so $z\mid ky^2$; since $z$ is coprime to $y$, $z\mid k$. Thus $c=kz\ge z^2\ge25$, achieved for $(3,4,5)$ with $k=5$: sides $15,20,25$, $AD=16$, $BD=9$, $CD=12$.

**Answer: 25**

smt-2012-geometry-tiebreaker-02.title: Cut and paste
smt-2012-geometry-tiebreaker-02.body:
Let $D,E,F$ be the midpoints of $BC$, $CA$, $AB$. $O_a$ passes through $E,F$; $O_b$ through $D,F$; $O_c$ through $D,E$ (right angles at the feet of midlines). The region $O_b\setminus(O_a\cup O_c)$ has vertices $D,E,F,B$; the sides $DE$ and $EF$ are concave arcs and $FB$ and $BD$ are convex arcs. Since $DEFB$ is a parallelogram, the arcs are congruent in pairs and the bulges fit into the dents, so the area equals that of parallelogram $DEFB$, which is $\frac12[ABC]$.

The rays $OA,OB,OC$ are at $0^\circ,60^\circ,150^\circ$, so $OABC$ is a convex quadrilateral and $[ABC]=[OAB]+[OBC]-[OAC]=\frac{\sqrt3}4+\frac12-\frac12\sin150^\circ=\frac{1+\sqrt3}4$. Half of it is $\frac{1+\sqrt3}8$.

**Answer: $\frac{1+\sqrt3}8$**

smt-2012-geometry-tiebreaker-03.title: Similar triangles and collinearity
smt-2012-geometry-tiebreaker-03.body:
All triangles $O_iO_{i+1}O_{i+2}$ are similar (sides $r_i+r_{i+1}$ etc. scale by $\frac12$ each step). Chasing angles shows $\angle O_iO_{i+2}O_{i+4}=\pi$, so the odd-indexed centers are collinear and the even-indexed centers are collinear. Hence the area of $O_1O_2O_n$ tends to the sum of areas $[O_iO_{i+1}O_{i+2}]$ over $i\ge1$.

$O_1O_2O_3$ has sides $\frac32,\frac54,\frac34$, i.e. $\frac14(6,5,3)$; by Heron ($s=7$) the $(6,5,3)$ triangle has area $\sqrt{7\cdot1\cdot2\cdot4}=2\sqrt{14}$, so $[O_1O_2O_3]=\frac1{16}\cdot2\sqrt{14}=\frac{\sqrt{14}}8$. Each next triangle has linear scale $\frac12$, so area ratio $\frac14$. Sum: $\frac{\sqrt{14}/8}{1-\frac14}=\frac{\sqrt{14}}6$.

**Answer: $\frac{\sqrt{14}}6$**
